clue.text: Stop by a humble dwelling

parts.note: to bung something is to stop or plug it
humble means low, modest in rank

explanation.surface: Someone halts beside a modest little house.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-storey detached house is a kind of home, so it is an example of a place to live.

clue.text: Talk incoherently without notes, but make a splash

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the talk goes round the notes

parts.note: to babble is to talk incoherently
E and D are both musical notes

explanation.surface: A speaker rambles without a script yet still manages to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it keeps its old sense of 'outside', so the talk surrounds the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedabble is to spatter or wet with drops, which is splashing.

clue.text: Coinage formerly found in rising flood

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, rising means the word for flood is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to flood is to drown
once means formerly, at one time

explanation.surface: Old money is discovered washed up in a mounting deluge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reads the flood word upwards, as it must in a down clue; 'found in' then places the old-time word inside it. A nonce word is coined for one occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made up for one occasion is a newly minted term, which is what coinage means for vocabulary.

clue.text: Fast forward

definitions.meaning: a clock that is fast is in front of the true time
forward means in front, further on

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean in front: a fast watch runs early, and going forward is moving to the front.

clue.text: Cheers as pub abandons modernising

indicators.note: abandons says the pub word is left out of the longer word

parts.note: innovation is the act of modernising
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A bar is applauded for refusing to update itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause from a crowd is a show of approval, the same sense as cheers as a noun.

clue.text: Minimal cover in bomb test site

definitions.meaning: a skimpy two-piece swimsuit covers very little
the Pacific atoll where the US tested atomic bombs

explanation.definitionFit: The swimsuit is named after the Pacific atoll used for American nuclear tests, so both senses share the name.

clue.text: Current local announced beer from the wood

indicators.note: announced says the word for local is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn
beer drawn from a cask rather than bottled is draught

explanation.surface: A pub serves cask ale, as broadcast on the news.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a neighbourhood pub in British usage; INN said out loud gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inward flow of air or water is a current drawn in.

clue.text: Firmly establish I have educational qualification

parts.note: read with the degree, 'I'm a BEd' says I have that qualification
BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A teacher proudly confirms they hold a teaching degree.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree; 'I'm a BEd' is another way of saying 'I have a BEd'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbed is a variant spelling of embed, to fix something deep and secure.

clue.text: I may have cowgirl over to eat

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means one piece sits above the next

parts.note: Io was the maiden Zeus turned into a heifer
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of inviting a cowgirl round for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Io, in Greek myth, was turned into a cow, so she is a 'cow girl'. I is the chemical symbol of the element.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the chemical symbol for the element, so the single letter stands for it.

clue.text: A Frenchman, father to French physicist

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a French man
pere is the French word for father

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is a father to a French person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampere was a French scientist who gave his name to the unit of electric current.

clue.text: English poet in fact French

definitions.meaning: a donnee is French for a given fact or premise

explanation.definitionFit: John Donne is the metaphysical poet, and in French a donne is a given, an established datum.

clue.text: Site for mosque had made mess — a builder's first to intervene

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so these letters go inside the others
a mess is a jumble, so these letters are rearranged
first picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A builder has bungled the construction of a place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' signals the anagram of the first two words, and 'to intervene' lodges the article and the builder's initial inside the result. The city is in Gujarat, India.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian city in Gujarat is famous for its historic Jama Masjid and many other places of Muslim worship.

clue.text: About to enter poor area of business, may end up on this?

indicators.note: to enter means the first piece goes into the second

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
re means about, concerning
a line is a field or trade, as in 'what's your line?'

explanation.surface: Someone moves into a struggling trade and fears ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the poverty threshold is the state of those barely able to eat, where a failing trader may land.

clue.text: Boy sees Opera North

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A lad goes to a performance by the Leeds-based company Opera North.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera North is an English opera company; here the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidan is a male first name, so a lad might bear it.

clue.text: After initial appearance, relative doesn't get involved

indicators.note: after says the relative comes behind the first piece

parts.note: a first look is how something initially appears
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: Once they have turned up, a family member stays out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch without taking part is to remain a spectator rather than a participant.

clue.text: Judicious cut produces this newsworthy quote

parts.note: sound means sensible, judicious
a bite is a cut taken out with the teeth

explanation.surface: Careful editing yields a quotable line for the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A short catchy extract from a speech, used in broadcasts, is a quotation made for the headlines.

clue.text: Some scores, being heavy, not opened

indicators.note: not opened means the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: weighty means heavy

explanation.surface: Some match results are heavy and remain sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Four scores make the number, a score being twenty.

clue.text: Time to get up? Put it off

parts.note: tempo is time in music, the speed of a piece
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: Is it time to get out of bed? No, delay it.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or delay so as to gain time.

clue.text: American doctor finally got computer link

parts.note: an interne is an American junior hospital doctor

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A US physician at last gets online.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide network connects computers, so it is a link between them.

clue.text: Tune gets a deserved hearing

indicators.note: a hearing means the phrase is listened to, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a just reward is a deserved one

explanation.surface: A melody finally receives the fair trial it merits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a just' said out loud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune an instrument or engine is to make small changes for correct working.

clue.text: Had not moved within easy reach

indicators.note: moved says these letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: Something was not shifted and stayed near at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close by is near enough to grab.

clue.text: The seat of empire?

parts.note: a seat of empire sounds like a capital, but this is a low padded couch named after a Turkish empire

explanation.definitionFit: The low upholstered footstool or couch takes its name from the Turkish empire.

clue.text: Classically rounded character

parts.note: a well-rounded person in the classics is really a round letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is the short O, a round letter in a classical script.

clue.text: Refuse-collector entirely captured in Dickensian character

indicators.note: captured in says one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a bin collects refuse
off means completely, as in finishing something off

explanation.surface: A dustman is perfectly portrayed in a Dickens role.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Boffin, the 'Golden Dustman' of Our Mutual Friend, really is a refuse collector, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Noddy Boffin is a figure in Dickens's novel Our Mutual Friend.

clue.text: University man forcibly ejected

parts.note: OU is the Open University
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: A college fellow is thrown out by force.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outed in the sense of expelled is to be thrown out.

clue.text: Volunteers nonsense, reading this?

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
rot is nonsense

explanation.surface: Some think fortune-telling is rubbish volunteered by believers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers give readings with these cards, so a reading may be of them.

clue.text: A single drop of the hard stuff?

definitions.text: A single drop of the hard stuff?

parts.words: A single drop of the hard stuff?
parts.note: a drop of hard stuff sounds like a nip of spirits, but it is a frozen pellet falling from the sky

explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice from a storm is one falling drop of frozen precipitation.

clue.text: Quench flames at last with water

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Put out a fire finally using water.
explanation.definitionFit: To slake thirst is to satisfy it, the same as quenching it.

clue.text: No Briton is in favour of incorporating rule by leader of Europe

indicators.note: incorporating means the first piece takes the rest into its middle

parts.note: for means in favour of

indicators.note: by means one piece stands next to the other

parts.note: to reign is to rule

indicators.note: leader of picks the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Eurosceptic Brit backs government from Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorporating' means the word for 'in favour of' is split open to take the rule word with E after it; 'No Briton' is a definition by negation.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from another country is not British, so an outsider.

clue.text: Hostile article contains malicious invention

indicators.note: contains says the article holds the other piece inside

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is a malicious invention

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece includes a spiteful falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien can mean opposed or repugnant, as in ideas alien to one's nature.

clue.text: New number that's lower

parts.note: something that numbs; ether was an early anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A fresh figure that is smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as 'numb-er', something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Concern making profit

definitions.meaning: a concern is a stake or involvement in something
money earned on a loan or deposit

explanation.definitionFit: A stake in something is a concern, and money paid on savings is a return on them.
